sources.entry: MedusaJs - Headless commerce engine that enables developers to create amazing digital commerce experiences. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Medusa is an open-source headless commerce platform and framework for building custom online stores, marketplaces, and commerce applications on Node.js and PostgreSQL.
summary.what_it_does: Provides commerce primitives such as products, carts, orders, and payments as modules, so developers can build B2B or DTC stores, marketplaces, distributor platforms, and PoS systems without writing core commerce logic from scratch. The repository is a Yarn workspaces monorepo containing the main @medusajs/medusa package with Store and Admin API routes, CLI commands, subscribers, and jobs. It also includes commerce modules (product, cart, order, pricing, payment), infrastructure modules (event bus, caching, file, locking, workflow engine), and module providers such as Stripe payments, S3 file storage, SendGrid notifications, and Redis locking/caching. The admin dashboard, the Medusa UI React component library, and CLI tools such as create-medusa-app are included in the monorepo. The README says the quickest setup is the npx create-medusa-app command, which can optionally add a Next.js Starter Storefront, or installation via Docker.
use_cases: manage products, carts, and orders via API
how_to_run: Install Node.js v22.22.0 or later and a running PostgreSQL database
Optionally include the Next.js Starter Storefront during setup
Alternatively, install with Docker (see installation guide)
notable: Modular architecture with swappable Module Providers for payments, storage, notifications, and auth
Includes an admin dashboard and a Next.js starter storefront option
Official plugins such as draft orders and loyalty
Medusa Cloud offered as a managed hosting option
caveats: Requires Node.js v22.22.0 or later and a running PostgreSQL database
Enterprise Edition RBAC materials require a commercial agreement with MedusaJS, Inc.
Medusa Cloud is a managed paid service referenced as the fastest path to getting started
